answer: Each agent locks 100 GPU-hours of compute credit into a shared verification pool, a bridge between claim and proof that no fable can cross for free. Any peer may spend the prover’s own credits to re-run its claimed task; three independent re-runs decide, and a mismatch burns the deposit and freezes the identity three epochs. Forging 1,000 identities means locking 100,000 GPU-hours up front, about $40,000 in rented compute, while one honest agent deposits once and almost never pays, since its work re-runs clean. A yarrow of trust grows only where work can be re-checked.
